title: Exclusive: Battery Smart raises $19.5 Mn at $430 Mn valuation
summary:
EV battery-swapping startup Battery Smart has raised Rs 185.5 crore or $19.50 million in its Series C funding round led by existing investors Rising Tide Ventures with the participation from Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures.

In March 2026, the company had raised Rs 66 crore in a pre-Series C round from Acacia Inclusion, Blume Ventures and PC-SBI Kurashi Visionary Fund, a funding round reported exclusively by Entrackr. This was followed by a $15 million debt funding from Mirova in April.
The board at Battery smart approved the allotment of 34,094 Series C CCPS at an issue price of Rs 54,407 each to raise the aforesaid amount, according to its regulatory filings with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Rising Tide Ventures led the round with Rs 112 crore or $11.8 million , followed by Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures which invested Rs 49 crore and Rs 25 crore respectively.

The Gurugram-based company raised the capital across two tranches, with the first tranche comprising nearly Rs 97 crore and the second tranche amounted at Rs 88 crore.

As per Entrackr’s estimate the company is valued at around Rs 4075 crore or $430 million post-money. The proceeds will be used to support business expansion, capital expenditure, working capital requirements, and other general corporate purposes, as per filings.
 
Founded in 2020, Battery Smart operates a battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers. Its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model allows users, particularly gig economy drivers, to swap batteries instead of bearing the high upfront cost of battery ownership.
 
The company has raised over  $211 million to date, with investors including Tiger Global, Blume Ventures and Ecosystem Integrity Fund.
 
As per the company’s regulatory filing, its revenue surged 43.8% to Rs 358 crore in FY26 from Rs 249 crore  in FY25, while loss declined by 12.8% to Rs 23.55 crore from Rs 27 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Atomberg’s early investors, founders sold Rs 683 Cr stake since 2019; A91 sold Rs 445 Cr
summary:
Consumer electronics startup Atomberg’s early investors, founders and other shareholders have sold shares worth around Rs 683 crore through secondary transactions since 2019, according to disclosures in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed ahead of its proposed IPO.
The transactions, spread across multiple years, show how Atomberg’s shareholder base has changed as the company raised more capital and brought in newer investors. Unlike a primary fundraise, where money goes into the company, these were share sales between existing and new shareholders, with the proceeds going to those who sold their shares.
A91 Emerging Fund I LLP was the biggest seller, offloading shares worth around Rs 445 crore. Another early investor, Parampara Early Stage Opportunities Fund Series I, sold shares worth about Rs 116 crore. Atomberg’s co-founders Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das also sold part of their holdings worth around Rs 71.6 crore. Meena sold shares worth about Rs 40.2 crore, while Das sold nearly Rs 31.4 crore.
However, the Rs 71.6 crore founder sale should not be added entirely on top of the Rs 683 crore figure, as around Rs 59 crore of the promoter transactions are already included in the broader secondary-sale data disclosed in the DRHP.

A large part of the shares sold by early investors was picked up by newer institutional investors. Temasek backed entities, Jongsong Investments Pte. Ltd and V-Sciences Investments Pte. Ltd  bought shares worth around Rs 187 crore and Rs 132 crore respectively. Funds linked to Inflexor also bought a significant portion of the shares sold by Parampara. Overall, the disclosed transactions involved around 14 sellers and 19 buyers.
Atomberg confirmed the figures to Entrackr.
The Rs 683 crore is not a fundraise by Atomberg. The money went to existing shareholders who sold their shares. This makes the transactions important for understanding how much liquidity early investors and founders have already taken out of the company and how ownership has shifted to newer investors over the years.
Founded by Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das, Atomberg started with energy-efficient BLDC ceiling fans and has since expanded into other home and kitchen appliances, including mixer grinders. The company has raised capital from investors including A91 Partners, Steadview Capital, Inflexor Ventures, White Whale and Temasek-linked funds as it expanded its product portfolio and distribution network.
As of the DRHP date, after selling worth Rs 445 crore of secondary shares, A91 Partners is still the largest shareholder in Atomberg with a 21.02% stake, followed by co-founder Manoj Kumar Meena with 17.73%. V-Sciences Investments and Jungle Ventures hold 11.8% and 10.03%, respectively, while co-founder Sibabrata Das owns 10.02%. Steadview Capital, Temasek-backed Jonsong Investments and Inflexor Ventures hold 7%, 6.98% and 6.08%, respectively.
On the financial front, Atomberg reported a 34.8% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 959.51 crore in FY25. However, its adjusted EBITDA improved to Rs 37.12 crore in FY26 from a negative Rs 51.35 crore in FY25. The company's net loss stood at Rs 149 crore in the previous fiscal.
The company is in last leg for its initial public offering, and the long trail of secondary transactions looks at how the company’s cap table has evolved from its early funding years to its current IPO phase, with some early investors, including A91 and Parampara, reducing their holdings while newer institutional investors have built positions.

summary:
Consumer appliances brand Atomberg’s revenue grew 34.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 1,294 crore in FY26, even as its losses widened during the year. The company’s revenue and financial performance details were disclosed in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP). 


The Mumbai-based company makes energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) and smart fans, along with mixer grinders, smart locks, water purifiers and juicers.
Home appliances remained Atomberg’s biggest revenue driver, contributing Rs 1,153 crore, or nearly 89% of its operating revenue, in FY26. Revenue from the segment grew 23.1% from Rs 937 crore in FY25.
The company’s kitchen appliances business saw sharper growth, with revenue jumping over sixfold to Rs 124 crore in FY26 from Rs 19.3 crore in the previous fiscal.
Atomberg also generated Rs 17.2 crore from proprietary components, compared with Rs 3.63 crore in FY25. Its other income stood at Rs 30 crore, taking its total income to Rs 1,324 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,001 crore a year earlier.
On the cost front, materials remained the company’s largest expense at Rs 738 crore, accounting for 50.55% of its total expenditure. The cost increased 37.9% from Rs 535 crore in FY25.
Employee benefit expenses also rose 32.1% to Rs 210 crore from Rs 159 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses stood at Rs 135 crore, while labour charges and depreciation and amortisation expenses came in at Rs 57 crore and Rs 71 crore, respectively.
Overall, Atomberg’s total expenditure increased 30.6% to Rs 1,460 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,118 crore in FY25.
The higher costs weighed on the bottom line, as the company’s net loss rose by 27.4% to Rs 149 crore from Rs 117 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs 50 crore from Rs 61 crore during the period.
Atomberg’s EBITDA margin improved to -3.86% in FY26 from -6.35% in FY25, while ROCE improved to -22.08% from -24.50%. The company spent Rs 1.13 to generate every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.16 in FY25. As of March 2026, Atomberg had current assets worth Rs 790 crore, including Rs 41 crore in cash and bank balances.


The company has today filed its DRHP. This comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 7.65 crore shares. 
Atomberg’s IPO comes as the company looks to scale its presence in the growing consumer appliances market. The company competes with established brands such as Havells, Crompton and Usha, while also expanding beyond its core fan business into other home and kitchen appliances.

The remaining proceeds will be deployed towards general corporate purposes.
Founded by Manoj Meena in 2012, Atomberg was joined by Sibabrata Das as co-founder in 2013. The company makes consumer appliances and components, with products spanning ceiling fans, mixer grinders, water purifiers, juicers and smart locks. title: Cashfree reports Rs 967 Cr revenue in FY26; losses narrow 23%
summary:
Following a flat scale in FY25, payments infrastructure and intelligence company Cashfree Payments staged a comeback in FY26, with its operating scale rising 51% year-on-year to nearly Rs 1,000 crore, while its losses narrowed by 23% during the year.
According to the company’s consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), Cashfree’s revenue from operations surged to Rs 967 crore in FY26 from Rs 640 crore in FY25.

Founded in 2015 by Akash Sinha and Reeju Datta, Cashfree Payments helps businesses collect online payments, make payouts, improve conversions, and streamline KYC and fraud detection. The company processes up to 12,000 transactions per second, handles over $80 billion in annual volume, and serves over a million businesses across sectors. 
The company also secured all three RBI payments licences: Payment Aggregator (PA-PG), Payment Aggregator-Cross Border (PA-CB), and Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI).
Payment gateway commissions remained the key revenue driver, contributing 92% of operating revenue in FY25. The segment saw an 85% jump in FY26, with revenue surging to Rs 890 crore from Rs 481 crore in FY25.
Payout commissions rose to Rs 69 crore, while cross-border payment commissions contributed another Rs 8 crore. Including around Rs 5 crore in other income, the Bengaluru-based company reported a total income of Rs 972 crore in FY26.
For the fintech firm, payment gateway processing costs accounted for 64% of total expenses, which rose by 66% to Rs 698 crore in FY26. Employee benefits expenses declined marginally to Rs 239 crore, while advertising and marketing costs fell 10% year-on-year to Rs 18 crore.
Other overheads, including depreciation and amortisation, finance costs, rent, domain charges, reseller commissions and software expenses, pushed Cashfree’s overall expenditure up 37% to Rs 1,091 crore in FY26.
A significant jump in payment gateway commissions, coupled with the growth in its merchant base and tighter control over other operating expenses, helped the firm narrow its losses by 23% to Rs 119 crore in FY26 from Rs 154 crore in FY25.
The Y Combinator-backed company’s EBITDA stood at Rs 90.5 crore in FY26, while its EBITDA margin improved to -9.36%. On a unit economics level, Cashfree spent Rs 1.13 to generate every rupee of operating revenue.

As on March 2026, Cashfree had total current assets of Rs 1,891 crore, including cash and bank balance of Rs 22 crore.
The company has raised $95 million from investors including Y Combinator, Smilegate Investments and State Bank of India, including a $53 million funding round led by Krafton in February last year.
Recently, the company appointed Sameer Gandhi as its new Chief Financial Officer and announced zero payment gateway fees for new businesses until March 2027.

summary:
New Delhi-based water infrastructure startup Neuromod Aqua has raised pre-seed funding from Porush Jain, founder of Sportskeeda.
The firm will use the capital, which is undisclosed, to build a factory-manufactured platform for decentralised sewage and effluent treatment.
Founded in 2026 by Anuj Arora and Anand Dad, Neuromod Aqua is developing modular wastewater treatment plants using technologies such as MBBR, MBR and SBR. The company is focusing on standardising the design, manufacturing, installation and servicing of treatment plants.
The startup plans to establish a manufacturing facility, develop and validate its productised sewage treatment plant, complete its initial commercial deployments and expand its process engineering and service capabilities.
India generates around 72,368 million litres of sewage per day, while installed treatment capacity stands at 31,841 MLD and actual treatment is around 20,235 MLD, according to the Central Pollution Control Board. Over the next 12 months, Neuromod plans to complete its manufacturing facility and initial deployments across Delhi NCR, while building a service and spare-parts network.

Prior to this, the Bengaluru-based startup had secured $3.2 million in a funding round led by Stellaris Venture Partners, with participation from angel investors including Maninder Gulati, V3 Ventures co-founder Arjun Vaidya, and others in August last year.

Founded last year by Chetan Sharma, Abhijit Gairola, and Vivek Khetan, Peeko operates a vertical quick commerce platform focused on baby and kids-care essentials. The platform offers apparel, diapers, toys, and baby food, along with try-and-buy and instant return options.
Peeko claims it has grown nearly two-fold every quarter over the past six months. More than one lakh parents have shopped on the platform since its launch. According to Peeko, it has expanded its assortment from around 6,000 SKUs at launch to 27,000-30,000 SKUs across apparel and accessories, toys and learning, baby gear, and consumables. Its average order value stands at around Rs 1,000, with apparel, toys, and baby gear accounting for a significant share of its business.

title: Y Combinator-backed Orange Health posts Rs 139 Cr revenue in FY26; loss nears Rs 100 Cr
summary:
Diagnostics and healthcare platform Orange Health is raising $30 million in fresh funding, with the impact of the capital infusion likely to reflect in its FY27 annual results. During FY26, the company’s revenue grew 65% year-on-year while losses widened to nearly Rs 100 crore as it expanded across tier I cities.
According to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), the Bengaluru-based startup’s revenue from operations surged to Rs 138.6 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 84 crore in FY25.

Founded in 2020 by Dhruv Gupta and Tarun Bhambra, Orange Health Labs is a full-stack diagnostics platform offering on-demand testing and at-home sample collection for routine diagnostics. Beyond D2C services, Orange Health has onboarded over 2,000 clinics on its platform to enable faster diagnosis and clinical decision-making.
The company claims to have added over 60 company-owned collection centres in the past year, with nearly 50 of them located in Bengaluru.
Diagnostics services remained the sole source of Orange Health’s operating revenue in FY26. It also earned Rs 4.7 crore from net gains on the sale of investments and other non-operating sources, taking its total income for the year to Rs 143 crore.
For the diagnostics firm, employee benefits was the largest cost, accounting for 30% of its overall expenses. The cost rose over 43% to Rs 72.2 crore during the fiscal year. Materials used for testing and diagnostics also increased 40% to Rs 42.9 crore.
Claims contract costs were another major expense for the firm, rising to Rs 35.8 crore in FY26, while its spend on marketing and advertising remained largely stable at Rs 34.4 crore. Rent, research and development, IT, legal and professional fees, along with other overheads, added another Rs 55 crore during the year. Overall expenses increased 36% year-on-year to Rs 240.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 175.9 crore in FY25.
The Bertelsmann India-backed company’s loss before tax increased 11% year-on-year to Rs 97 crore during the year. The company also booked a deferred tax expense of Rs 49 crore, which took its overall loss to Rs 146 crore.
Meanwhile, the company’s EBITDA loss stood at Rs 92.4 crore, with an EBITDA margin of -66.68%. However, the firm claims to have achieved 20% EBITDA profitability in Bengaluru.

On a unit level, it spent Rs 1.73 to earn a single rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As at March 2026, Orange Health had total current assets of Rs 55 crore, including Rs 4.5 crore of cash and bank balance. 
Prior to its $30 million round, Orange Health Labs had raised nearly $50 million in funding. The company raised $12 million in 2024 in a round led by Amazon Sambhav Venture Fund, followed by a $25 million Series B round in 2022 led by General Catalyst and Bertelsmann India Investments.
Orange Health competes with PharmEasy-owned Thyrocare, which reported Rs 829 crore in revenue and Rs 163 crore profit in FY26. Meanwhile, Redcliffe Labs posted Rs 419 crore in revenue in FY25. Healthians reported Rs 263 crore revenue in FY25 and narrowed its loss to Rs 5 crore. Their FY26 financials have yet to be filed.

title: Exclusive: BGauss raises Rs 110 Cr in fresh round at Rs 1,000 Cr valuation
summary:
Electric two-wheeler maker BGauss has raised Rs 110 crore ($11.6 million) in a Series D funding round led by founder Hemant Mahendrakumar Kabra, with participation from existing investor Bharat Value Fund and others.
The board of BGauss has approved the allotment of 17,26,846 Series D CCPS at Rs 637 per share, including a face value of Rs 10 and a premium of Rs 627 per share, to raise the aforesaid amount, according to a regulatory filing sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Kabra led the round with an investment of Rs 50 crore, while existing investor Bharat Value Fund infused Rs 44 crore. Adesh Realtor LLP and Maithan Alloys contributed Rs 10 crore and Rs 6 crore, respectively.
The latest round values BGauss at around Rs 1,000-1,100 crore on a post-money basis, giving the company fresh capital to scale its operations, strengthen its product portfolio and support its expansion plans.
The fresh funding could be part of a larger round, and the valuation may vary accordingly.
Founded in 2020 by Hemant Kabra, BGauss makes electric scooters that combine design with technology features such as AI-enabled systems, IoT integration, fast charging and low-maintenance requirements.
The company registered 5,518 retail registrations in July 2026, marking around 3X year-on-year growth. BGauss held a 0.3% share of India’s electric two-wheeler market during the month.
BGauss operates in an increasingly competitive electric two-wheeler market. It competes with startups and new-age EV players such as Ather and River Mobility, along with established players including Ola Electric, Hero MotoCorp, TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto.
Previously, BGauss had raised $18.6 million in funding from Bharat Value Fund (BVF) in January last year. Earlier in April 2022, it had raised Rs 52 crore (around $6 million) from a group of investors led by Darshan Patel, founder of Vini Cosmetics Pvt. Ltd.
The fresh funding comes at a time when India’s electric two-wheeler market is witnessing growing competition, with manufacturers stepping up investments in products, technology and distribution to capture a larger share of the market.

title: Yantra Packs raises Rs 12 Cr in seed round led by Caret Capital
summary:
Yantra Packs, a technology-driven asset-pooling and reusable packaging platform, has raised Rs 12 crore in a seed funding round led by Caret Capital.
The Gurugram-based startup had earlier raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed round from Impact Infracap in December 2024.
The fresh funds will be used to expand across India, strengthen its technology capabilities and scale its reusable packaging asset pool, Yantra Packs said in a press release.
Founded in 2020 by Vipin Battu and Karan Saharan, Yantra Packs provides reusable packaging assets such as pallets, crates, containers and other returnable transport items through asset rental and pooling models.
Its technology platform, Trakkia, enables asset tracking and supply-chain visibility, helping enterprises improve asset utilisation, manage asset lifecycles and reduce packaging-related costs and losses.
Yantra Packs claims to serve over 30 enterprise customers, with more than 250,000 containers in active circulation across eight warehouses and over 100 customer touchpoints spanning manufacturing clusters.
It competes directly with the other companies in this space such as Leap India, Holisol logistic, Econovus, and Good pack.
The reusable packaging sector has also seen fresh investor interest. Econovus Packaging raised Rs 40 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter, with participation from Rockstud Capital. InfinityBox also raised Rs 14.1 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter.

title: Navi raises $100 Mn from Prosus ahead of IPO
summary:
Fintech unicorn Navi has raised $100 million from Prosus. This is the company’s first institutional funding round and the transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals, including clearance from the Competition Commission of India (CCI).
Prosus said it was attracted to Navi’s large user base, multiple business lines, technology-first approach and focus on consumer experience. It also added that Navi has executed well over the past 12 months despite a tough macro environment.
While Navi did not disclose the valuation, an ET report pegs it at around $1.3 billion. It is worth noting that Navi had been seeking external funding at a $2 billion valuation for some time, according to media reports.
Founded by Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal, Navi operates across lending, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments. In March 2026, Navi launched motor insurance as part of its insurance portfolio. 
In February 2025, Navi appointed Rajiv Naresh as CEO of Navi Technologies and Abhishek Dwivedi as CEO of Navi Finserv, while Sachin Bansal moved to the role of Executive Chairman of the Navi Group.
The investment comes a few months ahead of Navi’s potential initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to target a valuation of around $2 billion.
Navi’s lending business faced a brief disruption in FY25 after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) paused new loan sanctions by Navi Finserv in October 2024 over compliance issues. The RBI lifted the curbs in December 2024.
During FY26, Navi UPI retained its position as India’s fourth-largest UPI app, while Navi Finserv’s assets under management (AUM) crossed Rs 13,000 crore. According to NPCI data, Navi held a 4% market share by transaction volume in July 2026.
Navi reported a net loss of Rs 466 crore in FY26, while revenue from operations rose 16% to Rs 2,982 crore. The company said it achieved consolidated profitability in Q4 FY26, supported by improving economics and operating leverage.
Navi offers loans, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments through its digital-first platform. The company said it has hundreds of millions of users across India and aims to build an integrated financial services platform for consumers.

title: Exclusive: Cashify to become public entity; appoints independent directors ahead of IPO
summary:
Cashify is taking concrete steps towards its proposed IPO, converting into a public company and appointing independent directors. The firm has also appointed IPO bankers and is expanding overseas, signalling that its public-market plans are moving into a more mature stage.
The board at Cashify passed a special resolution to change its name from Cashify Private Limited to Cashify Limited, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
As part of its IPO preparations, Cashify has appointed Vipul Sabharwal and Anil Berera as non-executive independent directors for a five-year term. Both directors will be eligible for remuneration of up to Rs 35 lakh each, including sitting fees.
In a separate resolution, the company also disclosed the salaries of its three co-founders, including perquisites, incentives and one-time bonuses. Mandeep Mancoha, Nakul Kumar and Amit Sethi received Rs 4.02 crore, Rs 4 crore and Rs 4 crore, respectively.
In March 2026, the company appointed ICICI Securities, JM Financial, and Nomura as bankers for its proposed initial public offering, according to a Moneycontrol report citing sources.
The company is also expanding its international operations. The board has also cleared the approval to establish Cashify Phone Trading FZCO, a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai Airport Free Zone, which will trade mobile phones, accessories, computers, refurbished goods, and other electronic devices.
Launched in 2013, Cashify allows users to buy and sell used electronics, with a primary focus on phones and laptops. The company partners with original equipment manufacturers such as Xiaomi, OnePlus, and Samsung to run exchange programmes. It also works with ecommerce giants Amazon and Flipkart to streamline the trade of refurbished devices for customers.
Cashify is yet to file its FY26 financial statements but its operational revenue reached Rs 1,096 crore in FY25 from Rs 935.07 crore in FY24. With revenue outpacing expenses, the company narrowed its losses by 80% to Rs 10.5 crore in FY25 from Rs 53 crore in the previous year.

title: CRED launches Circle app to connect members with experienced peers
summary:
Fintech platform CRED has launched Circle by CRED, a new app that allows its members to have one-on-one conversations with experienced professionals, founders and specialists across careers, money, wellness and relationships.
The service is currently in beta for select CRED members, with more than 100 Residents across these categories. Members can connect with Residents through text, audio or video between 6 PM and 10 PM, seven days a week. Pricing starts at Rs 25 per minute.
In simple terms, Circle is a paid advice platform where CRED members can speak directly with people who have relevant experience in a particular area. A founder, for instance, can speak with an experienced founder about leadership hiring or fundraising. A product leader can seek advice on a career transition, while a relationship specialist can help a member with their dating profile.
CRED said Residents are selected based on their relevance, credentials and experience. Members can have a one-time conversation or return to the same Resident for more complex discussions.
The platform is built on CRED’s 1.7 crore-member community. CRED describes this base as a group of affluent Indians with experience across different fields.
Miten Sampat, interim CEO at CRED, said, “Information and intelligence are abundant now, but judgement and taste are still developed through experience. For our affluent members, the collective experience of qualified peers is now a conversation away, with a high-signal network on Circle by CRED to enable their progress.”
Circle will expand into more categories over time. Select CRED members can access the beta, while other CRED members can download the app on iOS or Android and join the waitlist. Members can also apply to become Residents.
The company said the long-term aim is to build a network where members can access the collective experience of the community.

title: Shiprocket makes stellar debut, shares list 35% above IPO price
summary:
E-commerce shipping and logistics platform Shiprocket made a strong debut on the stock exchanges on Wednesday, August 19, with its shares listing at Rs 131 on the NSE, a 35% premium over its issue price of Rs 97.
The company’s shares were listed at Rs 131 on the NSE and Rs 130 on the BSE, giving investors a solid listing gain on the first day of trading.
Shiprocket had fixed the price band for its IPO at Rs 92-97 per share. The Rs 1,617 crore public issue was open for subscription between August 12 and August 14 and saw strong demand across investor categories.
The issue included a fresh issue of shares along with an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders. Shiprocket had earlier planned a larger IPO of around Rs 2,342 crore, but later cut the issue size to Rs 1,617 crore.
The IPO was subscribed 99 times by the end of the bidding period. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion 123 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) quota was subscribed 89 times, while the retail portion saw 46 times subscription. The employee portion was subscribed 55 times.
The strong debut comes as Indian startups continue to test investor appetite in the public markets. Shiprocket joins a growing list of new-age companies tapping the IPO route to raise capital and provide an exit opportunity to existing investors.
The Gurugram-based company provides shipping, logistics and ecommerce enablement services to online sellers and businesses. It is backed by investors including Temasek and Eternal.
Shiprocket reported a 24% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 2,024 crore in FY26. However, its net loss widened 6.8% to Rs 79 crore during the year.

Y Combinator was an early backer of Groww and has benefited significantly from the company’s growth and public-market debut. The accelerator continues to hold a sizeable 7.44% stake even after the latest transaction.

title: Exclusive: Krafton-backed Bobble AI enters insolvency process after failing to repay debt
summary:
Bobble.AI, the homegrown AI-powered communication and data intelligence startup, has entered insolvency proceedings.
The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), New Delhi, has admitted an insolvency plea against Talent Unlimited Online Services Private Limited, the legal entity behind Bobble AI, and started the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) against it, as per the filing sourced from the RoC.
The order was passed on June 12 on a petition filed by Axis Trustee Services Limited, which was acting as debenture trustee for a group of investors.
As per the filings, the tribunal has appointed Manish Agarwal as the Interim Resolution Professional (IRP) and declared a moratorium on the company. This means no legal action, asset sale, or recovery can happen against Bobble AI for now.
According to the order and regulatory filings, Bobble AI had raised Rs 25 crore in March 2023 by issuing secured debentures to investors. The company started missing repayments from August 2025.
With interest included, the total default stood at around Rs 5.77 crore. The security created against these debentures was also registered with the RoC, as per the filings.
Bobble AI had argued that since talks with lenders were still going on, the default should not count yet. The tribunal did not accept this and said the company's own emails clearly admitted the debt and default.
Entrackr has reached out to Bobble AI founder Ankit Prasad for a comment and will update this story once we hear back.
Bobble.ai offers an AI-powered Indic keyboard supporting over 120 languages, with facial recognition for personalized GIFs and stickers. Integrated with WhatsApp and Facebook (Meta), the company monetizes through ads, data insights, subscriptions, and branded merchandise.
The Gurugram-based company has raised around $35 million, including $26 million in a mix of primary and secondary capital from Krafton Inc in September 2022. Krafton controls a nearly 25% stake in the 12-year-old company.
Last year, the company also laid off around 50 employees amid restructuring. Entrackr exclusively reported the development.

title: Swiggy shareholders approve 49.5% foreign ownership cap
summary:
Swiggy shareholders have approved a proposal to cap the company’s aggregate foreign ownership at 49.5% at its 13th Annual General Meeting (AGM) held on August 18, 2026, clearing a key hurdle in its transition to an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC).
The approval comes after Swiggy’s domestic ownership crossed 50% in July, with foreign ownership at 49.76%. This includes foreign direct investment (FDI), foreign portfolio investment (FPI) and other indirect foreign investments. Swiggy had earlier sought shareholder approval for the IOCC transition in May, but the proposal failed to secure the required votes.
The IOCC status is particularly important for Swiggy’s quick commerce arm Instamart. Once the company completes the transition, Instamart could move towards an inventory-led model, similar to Eternal’s Blinkit.
Under the inventory model, Instamart could directly purchase and own products sold through its platform rather than operating purely as a marketplace connecting sellers and consumers. This could also allow Swiggy to recognise the full value of sales as revenue instead of earning only commissions from sellers.
Eternal had adopted a similar structure for Blinkit after its foreign ownership fell below the 50% threshold. The shift helped Blinkit move towards an inventory-led model and changed the way the quick commerce business reported its revenue.
In Q1 FY27, Swiggy reported 7% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue to Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4,961 crore in Q1 FY25. The company also narrowed its losses by 34% to Rs 791 crore during the period.
Swiggy earlier today expanded the roles of three senior executives across its Instamart and Food Marketplace businesses. Himavant Kurnala was named Chief Growth and Product Officer at Instamart, Nitesh Garg as its CTO, while Saurav Goyal took charge as COO of the Food Marketplace.
Swiggy’s shares closed at Rs 274 on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 75,633 crore ($7.96 billion).

title: Swiggy names new CGPO and CTO for Instamart; appoints COO for Food Marketplace
summary:
Foodtech and quick commerce platform Swiggy has expanded the roles of three senior executives across its Instamart and Food Marketplace businesses.
Himavant Kurnala has been appointed Chief Growth and Product Officer at Instamart, while Nitesh Garg has been named Chief Technology Officer at Instamart. Saurav Goyal has taken charge as Chief Operating Officer of the Food Marketplace.
Kurnala has led Instamart’s product function since 2024 and later took on growth and brand marketing. In his expanded role, he will oversee Growth, Marketing, Analytics and Product.
Garg has been with Swiggy for more than seven years and most recently served as Senior Vice President, leading engineering for Instamart and New Initiatives. He will now oversee technology for Instamart.
Goyal joined Swiggy in 2020 and has held roles across Business Finance for Food and Instamart, as well as Driver and Delivery Product and Operations. As COO of the Food Marketplace, he will also oversee Food Customer Experience while continuing to lead Driver and Delivery.
The appointments come amid a series of leadership changes at Instamart. Former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha was appointed CEO of Instamart effective August 3, succeeding Amitesh Jha, who resigned to pursue other opportunities.
Sinha’s appointment followed the exits of other senior executives, including COO Ankit Jain and CBO Hari Kumar. Jain recently joined Nykaa to lead its quick commerce business, Nykaa Now.
Earlier this year, Swapnil Bajpai was elevated to CEO of Swiggy’s Dineout and Scenes business. Sidharth Bhakoo continues as Chief Business Officer of the Food Marketplace, while Gautam Swaroop is the Chief Business Officer of Instamart.

title: DSP Finance acquires Volt Money to strengthen digital lending platform
summary:
DSP Finance, the NBFC arm of DSP Group, has acquired Salter Technologies, which operates digital lending platform Volt Money. The platform provides loans against financial assets, including Loans Against Mutual Funds (LAMF).
The acquisition combines the two businesses in the secured lending space. DSP Finance brings its balance sheet, risk management capabilities and institutional infrastructure, while Volt Money brings its digital lending platform and distribution network.
Volt Money enables customers to borrow against their mutual fund holdings, with funds disbursed within five minutes, subject to applicable processes and approvals. The acquisition will help DSP Finance expand its digital lending offerings against financial assets and serve customers across the mutual fund and wealth management ecosystem.
DSP Finance said it has built a presence in digital lending since receiving its NBFC registration in July 2024. The company has onboarded more than 1.8 lakh retail customers and built a loan book of around Rs 4,000 crore.
LAMF allows investors to access liquidity against their mutual fund holdings without redeeming their investments. This enables investors to meet short-term liquidity requirements while remaining invested in their long-term assets. With mutual funds and other financial assets accounting for a growing share of Indian household wealth, loans against such assets are emerging as an alternative source of credit.
Founded in 2022 by Ankit Agarwal, Bharat Lamba and Lalit Bihani, Volt Money enables customers to borrow against their mutual fund holdings. The company focuses on providing digital access to credit against financial assets.

title: NeoGeo raises $20 Mn Series A led by Neev II Fund and Aavishkaar Capital
summary:
Geospatial technology startup NeoGeo has raised $20 million in a Series A funding round led by Neev II Fund and Aavishkaar Capital, the investment arm of Aavishkaar Group.
The company said in a press release that it will use the funds to expand its platform and product portfolio through investments in R&D and technical capabilities, enter international markets across the Middle East and the Americas, and strengthen its team to support its pipeline of projects.
According to market research, India’s geospatial sector was valued at Rs 45,000 crore ($5.1 billion) in 2023 and is projected to grow at over 15% CAGR between 2025 and 2030.
Founded in 2019 by Sreeramam GV, NeoGeo is a full-stack geospatial technology system integrator that provides GIS-referenced platforms and solutions across urban governance, infrastructure and utilities, and natural resource management.
The company has executed over 200 projects, mapped more than 5 lakh sq km and manages over 550 CORS stations. It also operates AI/ML-based analytics platforms that help governments and enterprises convert spatial data into decision-ready intelligence.
According to the Gurugram-based company, it operates across the geospatial value chain, from data acquisition using satellite imagery, LiDAR, drones and ground surveys to data processing, AI/ML-based analytics and industry-specific software platforms. Its proprietary platforms include OptiFleet, GeoBalance, UrbanVista and InfraSync.
NeoGeo said its solutions are used for spatial planning and resource efficiency, as well as climate mitigation and resilience through hazard and vulnerability mapping.
The Indian geospatial sector includes startups such as SatSure, Pixxel, GalaxEye, SkyServe and Heliware, which are developing capabilities across Earth observation, hyperspectral imaging, spatial intelligence and location-based analytics.
Gurugram-based Heliware raised Rs 4.5 crore in a bridge round led by Inflection Point Ventures in February 2026. SatSure secured a Rs 24.6 crore grant from IN-SPACe in June 2026 to develop AI-powered Earth observation models and a sovereign geospatial intelligence backbone. Hyderabad-based TakeMe2Space also raised $5 million in January 2026 to expand its satellite constellation and real-time in-orbit AI capabilities.

title: Uber partners with ixigo to offer train ticket booking on Uber app
summary:
Multinational transportation company Uber has launched train ticket booking on its app in partnership with AI-native travel platform ixigo.
The offering allows users to book train tickets, check PNR status and connect their first- and last-mile journeys through Uber, bringing these services together on a single app.
The launch is part of Uber’s expansion of its intercity travel offerings in India. Through the partnership, ixigo will provide its train ticket booking technology and post-booking services, while Uber will connect train journeys with its mobility services.
Uber already operates at railway stations across India, and the new feature extends its services beyond station connectivity to train ticket booking.
With the addition of train ticket booking, Uber’s mobility portfolio in India now spans moto, auto, cars, metro, intercity cars, intercity buses and train ticketing. Uber entered India in 2013 and currently operates in more than 225 cities.
Founded in 2007 by Aloke Bajpai and Rajnish Kumar, ixigo is a travel technology company that enables users to plan, book and manage trips across trains, flights, buses and hotels. Its ixigo, ConfirmTkt and AbhiBus apps offer travel booking and utility services, including train, flight, bus and hotel bookings.

title: Health-tech platform Lissun raises Rs 48 Cr in Series A led by Colossa Ventures
summary:
Lissun, a single-specialty health-tech platform focused on children with special needs and developmental delays, has raised Rs 48 crore in a Series A funding round led by Colossa Ventures.
The round saw participation from Physis Capital and existing investors including RPSG Capital Ventures, Ivycap Ventures, Rainmatter, Multiply Ventures and SucSEED Ventures. New investors New Age India Fund and Beyond Capital Ventures also participated in the round.
The Gurugram-based startup had previously raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by RPSG Capital Ventures in September 2024. It also raised Rs 2.77 crore from Zerodha and other investors in June this year.
The fresh capital will be used to expand Sunshine by LISSUN centres in key cities, develop AI-led solutions using its proprietary technology and data, and strengthen clinical processes across its network, Lissun said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Krishna Veer Singh and Tarun Gupta, Lissun operates through its child-care brand Sunshine by LISSUN, which runs child development centres across India along with digital products and AI-led tools.
The company said it has grown fourfold over the past year and currently conducts more than 10,000 therapy sessions each month across 25 centres. It plans to expand its physical network to 50 centres by next year, while its digital products are targeted at reaching more than 10 lakh children over the coming years.
India is witnessing a growing need for advanced developmental and behavioral care for children, but access to high quality, consistent care remains sparse and fragmented. Lissun is bridging this gap through its child care brand, Sunshine by LISSUN, bringing together high-quality therapists and an AI-led ecosystem accessible both at centers and digitally.
Lissun competes with platforms such as Butterfly Learnings, Continua Kids, Hoola Health and Children First from Amaha.
The single-specialty health-tech segment focused on children with special needs and developmental delays has seen the emergence of startups working across early screening, diagnosis support, therapy and long-term developmental care for conditions including autism, ADHD, and speech and language disorders.
Butterfly Learnings raised Rs 32 crore in Series A funding in 2024, while CureAble secured Rs 2 crore in pre-seed funding in 2025. Gabify raised $175K in pre-seed funding in 2026. More recently, paediatric healthcare platform Hoola Health raised $5 million in 2026 and offers developmental assessments and therapy services as part of its child-focused care model.

title: Razorpay launches AI payments model Vulcan with NVIDIA and AWS
summary:
Fintech unicorn Razorpay has launched Vulcan, an AI foundation model built specifically for payments, with technology support from NVIDIA and AWS.
The Bengaluru based company said the transformer based model has been trained on nearly 3 trillion data points across 4 billion payments and uses around 3,000 signals per transaction to make payment related decisions.
NVIDIA GPUs were used to train and run the model, while AWS cloud infrastructure and Amazon SageMaker supported its development, training and deployment.
Razorpay said Vulcan is designed as a common intelligence layer for payment functions such as routing, fraud detection, risk assessment and checkout personalisation, replacing separate models for individual functions.
Components of the model were already being tested on Razorpay’s network ahead of the launch. Customers including Blinkit, Bachatt and redBus have started using some of these capabilities in live payment environments.
Razorpay claims the technology has improved payment success rates by 8-10% and helped detect and stop 8x more international card fraud. It has also identified five times more fraudulent or disputed transactions without increasing the number of alerts.
Through Magic Checkout, the company said 40% more shoppers are now shown their preferred UPI app, helping complete an additional 1-2 lakh purchases every month.
The model draws on signals across merchants, payment instruments, issuers and gateways to assess payment routes and select the one most likely to succeed. It can also identify fraud patterns across merchants, assess risks associated with cash on delivery orders and recommend payment methods during checkout.
Razorpay said Vulcan has been developed from the ground up, with its architecture and training data being proprietary.
The company’s internal study across 1.5 million shoppers and more than 51,000 businesses found payment friction such as failed transactions, delays and drop offs across metro and smaller markets.
Razorpay plans to expand the model to other areas, including authentication and lending, as it looks to use a single AI layer across more payment decisions.
The launch comes as India’s digital ecommerce market is projected to reach $350 billion by 2030, according to Razorpay.

title: Norwest leads $12.5 Mn Series A round in AI lending-tech platform Rezolv
summary:
Rezolv, an AI-native lending technology platform for financial services, has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Norwest, with participation from Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia and India and existing investor 3one4 Capital.
Prior to this, the Mumbai-based firm had raised $3.5 million in a seed round led by 3one4 Capital in March last year.
The company will deploy the fresh capital to strengthen its core AI capabilities across the lending suite, including sales, risk, underwriting and collections, Rezolv said in a press release.
Co-founded in October 2024 by Karan Mehta and Sonali Jindal, who were also the co-founders of digital lending startup Kissht, Rezolv is a lending-tech platform that enables lenders to automate, streamline and optimise their lending workflows. From welcome calling and pre-delinquency to write-offs, the platform leverages advanced analytics, automation and digital engagement to drive efficiencies while improving customer experience.
Rezolv serves banks and NBFCs through a debt-collection platform powered by AI, combining lending and collections expertise with an AI-first technology stack. The startup aims to build end-to-end automation for lending workflows.
Since its inception, Rezolv claims to have partnered with over 22 banks and NBFCs, including AU Small Finance Bank, ICICI Bank, Poonawalla Fincorp, Bajaj Auto Credit and Five-Star Business Finance. It powers 6.5 million minutes of borrower conversations every month, enabling pan-India collections across more than 12 million loan accounts. The company claims its platform has helped improve bounce and resolution rates by 35%.
Rezolv competes with players such as Credgenics, Nucleus Software, and Mobicule in the AI-powered lending and debt collections space.

title: Wispr Flow raises $280 Mn at $2 Bn valuation
summary:
San Francisco-based voice AI startup Wispr Flow has raised $280 million in a Series B funding round led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from existing investors including Notable Capital, NEA, Neo Ventures and 8VC. 
New investors include Acrew, Forerunner, Goodwater and Peak XV. The round valued the company at $2 billion. 
The fresh funding takes Wispr Flow’s total capital raised to $361 million. The company had raised $25 million at a $700 million valuation less than a year ago, making the latest round a near threefold increase in valuation. 
The new capital will be used to expand its product and speech AI capabilities. The company has also introduced Canto, its proprietary speech recognition model, which is designed to improve accuracy in difficult environments. 
Founded by Tanay Kothari, Wispr Flow develops AI-powered speech-to-text software that allows users to write and perform workplace tasks using voice. The company said its platform is used by more than 10,000 businesses. 
Recently, Kothari said that India is the second-largest market for Wispr Flow in terms of both users and paying subscribers.
The company is also expanding beyond voice dictation into areas such as meeting notes and other workplace applications. Peak XV’s participation marks its entry as a new investor in the company.

title: Milky Mist makes strong debut, lists at 18% premium
summary:
Dairy products company Milky Mist made a strong debut on the stock exchanges on Monday, with its shares listing at a 17.86% premium over the IPO price.
 
The company’s shares opened at Rs 165 on the National and Bombay stock exchanges, compared with the issue price of Rs 140. 
 
Milky Mist Dairy Food’s IPO was a Rs 1,553 crore issue, comprising a Rs 1,428 crore fresh issue and a Rs 125 crore offer for sale (OFS) by promoter shareholders. The company fixed the IPO price band at Rs 133–140 per share, with the issue open for subscription from August 11 to 13, 2026.
 
Milky Mist’s IPO was subscribed 56.12X, with QIBs showing the strongest demand at 155.83X. NII and retail portions were subscribed 34.91X and 8.41X, respectively.
 
The company has also raised around Rs 482 crore in a pre IPO funding round from Jongsong Investments Pte Ltd, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Temasek Holdings, according to a public announcement. 
 
The company operates in the value-added dairy segment, with products across categories including dairy-based foods and beverages. Its growth strategy also includes expanding its manufacturing capacity, distribution network and product portfolio.
 
Milky Mist reported a 33.6% YoY growth in revenue to Rs 3,138.36 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,349.50 crore in FY25, while its profit surged 175.7% to Rs 127.01 crore from Rs 46.07 crore.
 
Milky Mist remains concentrated in its home market, with around 69.23% of FY26 revenue coming from South India. Around 94.51% of its raw milk procurement also came from Tamil Nadu, leaving the company exposed to regional concentration.
 
The company is currently trading at Rs 181.5 (as of 10.16 AM) with a total market capitalization of Rs 13,972 crore.

title: Superhealth appoints former Dunzo co-founder Dalvir Singh Suri as head of operations
summary:
Superhealth has appointed Dalvir Singh Suri, former co-founder of Dunzo, as its head of operations as the healthcare startup prepares to scale its hospital network across India.

At Superhealth, Suri will focus on building the systems, teams and operating processes required to replicate the company's healthcare model across multiple locations. The startup plans to expand from its flagship Bengaluru hospital to 100 multispecialty hospitals across India over the next five to seven years.
Superhealth operates on a zero-wait and zero-commission model, with full-time salaried doctors, fixed all-inclusive pricing and digitally managed clinical and operational workflows. Its proprietary SuperOS uses AI to support hospital operations, including real-time patient monitoring and clinical audits.
The company claims that its Bengaluru hospital has recorded an average length of stay that is nearly one-third of that of a typical corporate hospital.
His appointment comes as Superhealth shifts from validating its first hospital model to building the operational infrastructure needed for a 100-hospital network.

title: upGrad crosses Rs 2,000 Cr gross revenue in FY26; EBITDA jumps 8X
summary:
Edtech major upGrad crossed the Rs 2,000 crore mark in gross revenue in FY26, while its bottom line improved sharply during the year amid continued cost control measures, as per the company's press release.
According to upGrad, gross revenue grew 7% year-on-year to Rs 2,070 crore in FY26, including taxes. Its total income stood at Rs 1,732 crore after Ind-AS accounting. The company also has Rs 530 crore in collected revenue that is yet to be recognised in future years.
upGrad’s Ind-AS EBITDA jumped more than eight times to Rs 123 crore from Rs 15 crore in FY25. Its net loss also narrowed 52% to Rs 130 crore during the year. The company said this is the third consecutive year in which its losses have more than halved year-on-year. The loss stood at Rs 1,142 crore in FY23.

The company said it had more than 100,000 concurrent learners across its online skilling, degree, study abroad and offline skilling businesses in FY26. Its B2B arm, upGrad Enterprise, also worked with more than 700 enterprises for employee skilling, recruitment and workforce development.
AI has also become a major part of the business, with the company saying that more than 80% of its programmes now include AI in their curriculum. It also said marketing and technology costs declined year-on-year despite revenue growth, helped by its use of AI in operations.
The improved bottom line comes as upGrad looks to expand its scale through acquisitions. The company said it is closing the acquisition of Unacademy and Internshala.
The Unacademy deal is expected to be one of upGrad’s biggest consolidation moves. Entrackr had reported in July that the all-stock transaction was valued at around Rs 1,955 crore and was expected to close within three weeks.
With the acquisition, upGrad aims to bring together its higher education and skilling business with Unacademy’s test preparation, medical education and creator-led learning platforms. The company said it now plans to focus on growth across India and global markets.

title: Vijay Shekhar Sharma-backed Resilient to sell 4.98% Paytm stake; Antfin to benefit
summary:
Vijay Shekhar Sharma-controlled Resilient Asset Management B.V. has proposed to sell up to a 4.98% stake in Paytm through a block market trade, according to a regulatory disclosure by One97 Communications.
The proposed sale will be carried out under an existing Optionally Convertible Debenture (OCD) agreement between Resilient and Antfin (Netherlands) Holding B.V., Paytm said in the disclosure.
Importantly, while Resilient will execute the share sale, the economic value from the transaction will be retained by Antfin under the OCD agreement.
Resilient had acquired around 10.20% stake in Paytm from Antfin in August 2023 against OCDs issued to Antfin. However, the economic interest in the shares continued to belong to Antfin, the company said.
The proposed transaction will therefore not result in any change in Vijay Shekhar Sharma’s direct shareholding in Paytm. The company also clarified that Paytm is not a party to the transaction.
The disclosure comes as Resilient seeks to monetise a portion of the Paytm shares held under the existing arrangement with Antfin. The proposed block trade could cover around 4.98% of Paytm’s equity.
In 2023, Resilient had acquired the stake from Antfin as part of a restructuring in Paytm. The deal was structured through OCDs, allowing Antfin to continue retaining the economic interest in the shares.
Paytm’s latest disclosure does not provide details on the proposed sale price, buyers or the expected value of the block trade. The transaction is subject to the terms of the existing OCD agreement between Resilient and Antfin.
At the end of today’s trading session, Paytm closed at Rs 1580 per share with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,01,312 crore ($10.6 billion).
